adjacent layers commonly differ in tone or texture density, creating a separated stratum-by-stratum appearance
less uniform and repetitive than striped or lined textures, with broader layer-like zones instead of narrow repeated marks
more clearly arranged in parallel stacked strata than marbled, which tends to swirl and branch

striped.position: a regular pattern defined by parallel elongated bands running in a consistent direction across the surface
family_visual_attributes: visible elongated linear elements or bands dominate the texture
elements are arranged with noticeable directional alignment
spacing between repeated linear elements is at least partly regular
the pattern extends across the image as a repeated motif rather than isolated marks
contrast is created by alternating lines, gaps, or differently colored elongated regions
distinguishing_visual_attributes: consists of multiple roughly parallel stripes with similar orientation across the image
the repeated elements are broader and more band-like than the thin marks typical of lined
the pattern does not form intersecting lattices or crisscrosses as in crosshatched
the stripes are generally straight or gently curved, not sharply angular back-and-forth forms like zigzagged
alternation between stripe and gap is the main structure, rather than wide irregular zones as in banded

studded.position: a texture defined by distinct protruding knobs or rivet-like points distributed across a surface, often in a fairly regular arrangement
family_visual_attributes: texture is built from many separate, countable small units rather than continuous lines or bands
units stand out clearly from the background by shape, shading, or contrast
surface often shows noticeable local relief with highlights and shadows around individual elements
elements tend to repeat across the image at similar size and spacing
overall appearance is spot-based or node-based rather than fibrous, striped, or smeared
distinguishing_visual_attributes: individual elements appear raised above the surface as bumps, studs, or rivet-like protrusions
studs usually have crisp, well-defined circular or rounded boundaries rather than soft flat spots
repeating protrusions are more discrete and isolated than the broader uneven swellings of bumpy textures
unlike pitted or perforated textures, the elements read as outward projections rather than holes or inward depressions

waffled.position: a highly regular grid-based texture with repeated recessed square or rectangular cells, forming a checker-like relief pattern
family_visual_attributes: repeated motif appears at regular intervals across the surface
elements are arranged in an ordered lattice or tessellation rather than randomly scattered
spacing between neighboring units is fairly uniform
pattern often shows clear horizontal and vertical alignment
overall texture reads as geometric and predictable at a glance
distinguishing_visual_attributes: contains a grid of sunken or raised cells that look like small pockets rather than just flat lines
cells are usually square or rectangular and separated by thicker ridges
pattern conveys visible surface relief or depth, unlike a purely printed grid
repeated units form a cushion-like checker of depressions rather than open holes or wire-like intersections
more blocky and orthogonal than hexagonal honeycombed or thin-line meshed patterns

woven.position: a structured interlaced texture formed by over-under crossing strands arranged into a repeated weave
family_visual_attributes: made of repeated linear elements that cross or loop around one another
shows a connected network rather than isolated marks or spots
contains many junctions where strands visually overlap or intersect
often has a regular repeating arrangement across the surface
creates small cells, gaps, or bounded spaces between crossing elements
distinguishing_visual_attributes: clear over-under weave pattern with alternating crossings visible along perpendicular strands
strands are usually relatively straight and arranged in two main directions rather than looping into rounded stitches
repeated rectangular or square units are common, but crossings look like layered bands rather than simple line intersections
surface often shows subtle relief at crossover points where one strand appears to pass above another

wrinkled.position: an irregular fold-and-crease texture defined by thin ridges and troughs formed by compressed or puckered surface undulations
family_visual_attributes: visible surface relief with alternating raised and recessed areas
elongated marks or bands created by deformation rather than discrete dots or cells
shading changes along ridges and valleys that emphasize depth
non-flat appearance with bends, puckers, folds, or compressed areas
texture structure is carried by continuous or semi-continuous crease-like features
distinguishing_visual_attributes: creases are irregular in spacing, thickness, and direction rather than evenly repeated
features appear as soft folds or puckers with rounded ridges, not sharp cut-like separations
pattern lacks the strong parallel order typical of pleated or lined textures
troughs usually remain connected by bent, rumpled surface undulations instead of deep channel-like grooves
creases often intersect or meander in a rumpled way without forming a stable grid or strict orientation

veined.position: an irregular network of thin, vein-like lines that branch and taper across a surface
family_visual_attributes: visible line elements dominate the texture rather than dots or large solid patches
lines form connected networks or pathways across the surface
line width is usually narrow relative to the spaces between them
the pattern is mostly irregular rather than perfectly repeating
junctions, forks, or directional changes appear within the line structure
distinguishing_visual_attributes: lines branch repeatedly in tree-like or river-like patterns rather than staying parallel
line thickness often tapers along segments, giving a natural vein-like appearance
the network is connected but not usually open-gap separated like cracked textures
the pattern lacks the broad swirls and blended color fields typical of marbled textures
intersections are mostly organic forks rather than the regular crossings seen in crosshatched or lined textures

swirly.position: a flowing, looped curvilinear texture defined by swirling arcs and curled turns rather than straight bands or angular repeats
family_visual_attributes: dominant curved or arcing lines rather than straight or angular marks
flowing directional paths that bend, loop, or meander across the surface
continuous visual rhythm formed by connected or closely related curved elements
orientation changes gradually along the pattern instead of abrupt directional breaks
pattern structure is organized by line movement more than by isolated dots, holes, or blocks
distinguishing_visual_attributes: contains repeated S-curves, curls, or whorl-like turns without needing full concentric spiral centers
the curved paths appear broad and flowing rather than thin branch-like tracery
motifs are less enclosed and teardrop-shaped than paisley forms
shows more obvious looping and rotational movement than marbled streaks, which look more diffuse and layered
lacks the clear central hubs and regular winding geometry typical of spiralled patterns

zigzagged.position: angular, repeating line pattern made of connected segments that reverse direction to form a sawtooth path
family_visual_attributes: texture is dominated by elongated linear marks rather than dots, holes, or blobs
lines create strong directional flow across the surface
adjacent elements often repeat with similar spacing or orientation
contrast is organized into bands, strokes, or paths rather than isolated specks
pattern structure is readable through edge alignment and line continuity
distinguishing_visual_attributes: lines bend sharply at repeated angles instead of remaining straight throughout
the main motif forms a back-and-forth sawtooth or serrated path with alternating diagonal segments
direction changes occur at regular intervals, creating pointed peaks and valleys
unlike chequered or crosshatched, the pattern is not primarily built from intersecting perpendicular grids
unlike striped or lined, the linear bands are broken by repeated angular turns rather than parallel straight runs
